config.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow

intro.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a solution to the Pacific Atlantic Water Flow lesson, which involves determining which cells on a grid allow water to flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans. You will learn the core programming concept of depth-first search (DFS) to traverse the grid from the ocean edges and track reachable cells. The main technologies and constructs involved include recursion, arrays, and conditional logic in JavaScript. By the end, you will understand how to apply DFS to solve grid-based flow lessons efficiently.
intro.usecase: The Pacific Atlantic Water Flow algorithm pattern appears in geographic information systems (GIS) and environmental monitoring dashboards where you need to identify areas affected by multiple sources. For example, in flood prediction software, developers implement this pattern to determine which coastal regions are vulnerable to water flowing from both ocean boundaries during storm surges. This same multi-source propagation logic is used in network analysis tools to find nodes reachable from multiple entry points, such as identifying server locations accessible from different data centers in infrastructure monitoring panels. Understanding this algorithm helps developers build more accurate environmental simulation tools and network visualization dashboards.

objectives: Implement a depth-first search function to traverse the grid from ocean boundaries
Construct two separate visited matrices to track Pacific and Atlantic ocean reachability
Initialize the search from all Pacific-adjacent cells and all Atlantic-adjacent cells
Manipulate the grid traversal to respect the water flow constraint (higher or equal elevation)
Integrate the Pacific and Atlantic reachability results to identify common cells
Render the final list of coordinates where water can flow to both oceans
Apply the algorithm to solve the Pacific Atlantic Water Flow lesson on various grid inputs

familyTeachingProfile.mentalModel: Remember what we have already seen
familyTeachingProfile.conceptBridge: Show the learner how to use a lookup structure (e.g. object or Map) to remember seen values and avoid re-scanning.
familyTeachingProfile.visualMetaphor: A notebook where we write down what we've seen and check it in one step.
commonConfusions: What do we store as key vs value?
When do we check the structure vs add to it?
